title: Italian Chopped Salad
source: Love and Lemons - Jeanine Donofrio (adapted from Gaby Dalkin)

components.name: Lemon Vinaigrette
components.why: Make it first so the shallot and garlic have a few minutes to mellow in the acid.
steps: Whisk everything together in a small bowl and set aside.

ingredients: 1 pint cherry tomatoes, halved or quartered
OPTIONAL: 5 pepperoncini, stemmed and sliced (jarred, in brine)
OPTIONAL: 4 oz Italian cured meat, cubed or torn - salami, soppressata, capicola or mortadella
steps: Make the lemon vinaigrette (above) and set it aside.
Halve the iceberg through the core, cut the core out, and slice lengthwise into 1/4-inch ribbons. Do the same with the radicchio.
In a large bowl combine the lettuce, radicchio, red onion, tomatoes, chickpeas, mozzarella and provolone.
Add the pepperoncini if you want the heat and tang, and the cured meat if you want it to eat like a meal.
Drizzle with the dressing and toss gently to coat.
Season with salt and pepper, toss again, sprinkle with the oregano and serve.
notes: PEPPERONCINI ARE OPTIONAL: jarred, packed in brine. They bring heat and vinegar - leave them out for a milder salad, or add a splash of their brine to the dressing instead if you want the tang without the bite. ITALIAN MEAT IS OPTIONAL: Gaby Dalkin's original has 4 oz cubed Genoa salami; Love and Lemons drops it to keep it vegetarian. Add about 4 oz of any Italian cured meat - salami, soppressata, capicola, mortadella - cubed or torn, and that turns this from a side into dinner. If you skip the meat, season more generously with salt, or add chopped sun-dried tomatoes or roasted red peppers for the same savory hit. DRESS IT LATE: iceberg and radicchio hold up better than most greens but leftovers are only good about a day before they wilt. Dress only what you are eating if you want it to keep. The red onion is in the original ingredient list but missing from its instructions - it goes in with the rest.

title: Fresh Basil Pesto
ingredients: 2 cups fresh basil leaves, packed (can sub half with baby spinach)
1/2 cup Romano or Parmigiano-Reggiano, freshly grated (about 2 oz)
1/8 tsp black pepper, more to taste
steps: Put the basil and pine nuts in a food processor and pulse a few times.
Add the garlic and cheese, pulse again, and scrape down the sides.
With the processor running, pour the olive oil in a slow steady stream - that is what emulsifies it and keeps the oil from separating later. Stop and scrape the sides once or twice.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Toss with pasta, dollop on a baked potato, or spread on toast or crackers.
notes: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan a few minutes first if you have the time - big flavor payoff, and it is the one thing the recipe leaves out. Pour the oil SLOWLY while the motor runs; dumping it in gives you a broken, oily pesto. Grate the cheese yourself, the pre-shredded stuff is coated in anti-caking starch and goes gritty. STORING: press into a jar, cover the surface with a thin layer of olive oil to stop it browning, refrigerate about 1 week. FREEZING: freeze in an ice cube tray, then bag the cubes - 2 cubes is about enough for one serving of pasta. If freezing, leave the cheese out and stir it in after thawing. PASTA: thin it with a splash of the starchy pasta water when you toss it, and do not heat it on the stove or it turns dull and bitter.

title: Miso Glazed Salmon
ingredients: Salt and pepper (go light - see notes)
1/4 cup miso paste (red; white also works)
Chopped green onions and sesame seeds, to garnish (optional)
steps: Season the salmon lightly with salt and pepper.
Whisk the miso, soy sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar and sesame oil in a small bowl until smooth. Set aside 1 Tbsp of the glaze for the end.
Toss the salmon with the remaining sauce and marinate 1-3 hours. Don't go past 3 hours - the texture breaks down.
Heat the oven to 375F. Scrape off and discard the marinade, set the fillets in a large oven-safe skillet, and bake 12-15 min until nearly opaque.
Brush with the reserved 1 Tbsp glaze and broil on high 1-2 min, until the center hits 125-130F.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Runs salty: use low-sodium soy sauce and skip or barely use the added salt - miso and soy both bring plenty. Marinate 1-3 hours only. Pull at 125-130F for moist, flaky fish; the broil at the end is what caramelizes the glaze.

title: Easy Pancake Batter
steps: Whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the milk, egg, melted butter and vanilla.
Pour wet into dry and stir just until combined - lumps are fine, don't overmix.
Let the batter rest 5 minutes.
Pour about 1/4 cup batter onto a hot, greased griddle over medium heat. Flip when bubbles form and the edges set; cook 1-2 min more per side.
notes: Use the Half / As written / Double buttons above the ingredients to switch batch size - the ingredient list and the add-to-grocery-list button both follow whichever one is selected. Yields: Half about 4 pancakes (2 people), As written about 8 (4 people), Double about 16 (8 people). The half batch still uses 1 whole egg, so it runs slightly richer than a true half - that is on purpose, half an egg is not worth the trouble. Overmixing makes tough pancakes. Swap in buttermilk plus a splash of lemon juice for extra fluffiness. Batter keeps 2-3 days refrigerated in an airtight container - stir before using, it loses some lift by day 2-3.

title: Slow Cooker Meatballs
servings: 4 (about 10 meatballs) - double it for a crowd
ingredients: 1/2 cup Pecorino Romano or parmesan, grated, plus more to serve
1 tsp kosher salt (see notes - the original calls for 1/2 Tbsp)
4-8 cloves garlic, peeled and left whole
Spaghetti or other pasta, to serve
steps: In a large bowl combine the ground beef, egg, breadcrumbs, diced carrot, diced onion, cheese, salt and pepper. Mix with your hands until evenly combined.
Roll into golf ball-sized meatballs. The mix looks vegetable-heavy - that is correct, the carrot and onion cook down and keep the meatballs moist.
Lay the meatballs gently in the bottom of the slow cooker, a second layer if needed.
Pour both cans (sauce and diced tomatoes) over the top, sprinkle on the oregano, and scatter the whole garlic cloves over that.
Cover and cook on LOW 6-8 hours. Stir gently with a wooden spoon halfway through.
Lift the meatballs out with a slotted spoon into a bowl. Taste the sauce and season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the sauce over pasta, top with the meatballs, and finish with grated cheese and parsley. Serve right away.
notes: SALT: the original calls for 1/2 Tbsp (1 1/2 tsp) and multiple readers found that too salty - 1 tsp is the safer start, and you season the sauce at the end anyway. Breadcrumbs are already seasoned and the cheese is salty. TIMING: 6 hours is usually enough; 8 is the outer edge. Doubling does not change the time. MAKE AHEAD: cook them a day early, refrigerate the whole insert, then put the insert back in the cooker on HIGH a couple of hours before dinner to reheat. SERVING: spaghetti is the default; also good as meatball subs or sliders, or over zucchini noodles. INSTANT POT (reader-tested, not the author): 7 min high pressure, 5 min natural release, then manual release. The printable card on the site leaves out the diced tomatoes - the full post includes them, and so does this version.

title: Marinated Pork Adobo (Tsingtao)
source: Tsingtao USA - Isabel Lee, Forsyth Fire Escape
steps: Pat the pork dry. Score both sides and cut between the skin and the meat so the marinade can get underneath.
Blend or crush the garlic into a paste.
Mix the garlic, paprika, onion powder, cumin, oregano, black pepper, salt, lime juice and oil into a marinade.
Rub the marinade all over the pork - including between the skin and meat and down into the cuts.
Set the pork skin-side up in a deep baking pan and pour the beer into the pan (not over the skin).
Cover with parchment paper, then seal tightly with aluminum foil.
Bake at 300F for 4 hours.
Remove the cover, raise the oven to 450F, and roast 10-15 min more until the skin crisps.
notes: From Isabel Lee of Forsyth Fire Escape, via Tsingtao USA. Feeds 15 - party roast, not a weeknight. The beer goes in the pan, not over the pork: it steams the meat from below while the skin stays dry enough to crisp at the end. Parchment first, then foil - foil straight on the meat reacts with the lime and salt. Cutting between skin and meat and rubbing marinade in there is what seasons it all the way through. Pull it out before the 450F blast only if the skin is already crisp; watch it, it goes from golden to burnt fast. Leftovers shred well for tacos.
